Links: [{"title":"GitHub - Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings: Sync MCP server configs from Claude Code to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, and Cursor — one command, all agents. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings"},{"title":"GitHub - holstein13/mcp-config-manager: Manage MCP server configs across Claude, Gemini & other AI systems. Interactive CLI for server enable/disable, preset management & config sync. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager"},{"title":"mcp sync","url":"https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync"},{"title":"mcp-sync 1.0.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md"},{"title":"Crate mcp_sync","url":"https://docs.rs/mcp-sync/latest/mcp_sync"},{"title":"GitHub - Abdalkaderdev/mcpport: See, lint, sync and convert MCP server configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport"},{"title":"GitHub - spyrae/agentsync: Sync MCP server configs and rules across AI coding agents · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/spyrae/agentsync"},{"title":"GitHub - eggboy/mcpshare: Sync MCP servers to different coding agents · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare"},{"title":"How to Add an MCP Server to Any AI Coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, Oh My Pi)","url":"https://inventivehq.com/blog/add-mcp-server-to-ai-coding-cli"},{"title":"Claude Code Supercharged: Access Any AI Model via MCP Integration - lgallardo.com","url":"https://lgallardo.com/2025/09/06/claude-code-supercharged-mcp-integration/"}]

Several open-source tools already do this. Most treat one existing config as the source, and the main pitfalls are format and key differences.

- **Claude Code as the source:** The sync-agents-settings tool describes itself as letting you configure MCP servers and write instructions once in Claude Code, then sync everywhere with a single command. agentsync reads from ~/.claude.json → global MCP servers and .mcp.json → project MCP servers.
- **A standalone canonical file:** mcp-sync reads a single `mcp.yaml` file and syncs the server definitions to Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity. mcpshare keeps a canonical mcp.json in a directory you choose.
- **Multi-tool editors:** mcpport covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor and can also lint and convert configs.

Config locations and formats differ across the three CLIs:
- Gemini CLI uses JSON at ~/.gemini/settings.json with a mcpServers key, and it preserves non-MCP settings.
- Codex uses TOML at ~/.codex/config.toml (global) or .codex/config.toml (project), with servers under [mcp_servers.*].
- HTTP endpoints use different keys: url in Claude/Codex/OMP, httpUrl in Gemini/Qwen.
- Some tools skip files they can't safely rewrite. mcpport reads but never writes a JSON target with comments (Gemini CLI allows them), because the rewrite would drop them.

Caveat: these are community projects I haven't verified. I didn't check their maintenance status, licenses, or whether they support the latest CLI versions. The search was a single query, so this is not a full survey.

Several open-source tools already do this. Most treat one existing config as the source, and the main pitfalls are format and key differences.

- **Claude Code as the source:** The sync-agents-settings tool describes itself as letting you configure MCP servers and write instructions once in Claude Code, then sync everywhere with a single command. agentsync reads from ~/.claude.json → global MCP servers and .mcp.json → project MCP servers.
- **A standalone canonical file:** mcp-sync reads a single `mcp.yaml` file and syncs the server definitions to Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity. mcpshare keeps a canonical mcp.json in a directory you choose.
- **Multi-tool editors:** mcpport covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor and can also lint and convert configs.

Config locations and formats differ across the three CLIs:
- Gemini CLI uses JSON at ~/.gemini/settings.json with a mcpServers key, and it preserves non-MCP settings.
- Codex uses TOML at ~/.codex/config.toml (global) or .codex/config.toml (project), with servers under [mcp_servers.*].
- HTTP endpoints use different keys: url in Claude/Codex/OMP, httpUrl in Gemini/Qwen.
- Some tools skip files they can't safely rewrite. mcpport reads but never writes a JSON target with comments (Gemini CLI allows them), because the rewrite would drop them.

Caveat: these are community projects I haven't verified. I didn't check their maintenance status, licenses, or whether they support the latest CLI versions. The search was a single query, so this is not a full survey.

**Install:** Requires Node 22+. Run `npx mcpport <command>` or install globally with `npm i -g mcpport`.

**Source of truth:** The page does not describe a single canonical config file. mcpport reads each agent's own config (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) and normalizes them into one internal shape. Claude Code is the reference format in the translation table, but the page doesn't name any file as the master copy.

**Sync:** `npx mcpport sync <from> <to>` copies servers that the source agent has and the target lacks. Examples on the page use `claude cursor`.
- Dry run by default; `--apply` writes.
- A server that exists in the target with a different definition is a conflict and is skipped unless `--force` is used.
- Entries that fail structural checks are reported as invalid and never copied.

**Supported targets:** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. The roadmap lists VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, and Claude Desktop as future agents.

**Preserves other settings:**
- JSON files: unrelated keys are kept when writing.
- Codex TOML: comments and unrelated tables are kept.
- Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`): non-MCP keys are kept.
- Keys a target format doesn't support (for example `startup_timeout_sec` or `trust`) are dropped during translation, and mcpport lists them.

**Backups and dry run:**
- Without `--apply`, sync is read-only.
- The target file is copied to `<file>.<timestamp>.bak` before it is written.
- Writes go through a temp file and rename.
- A target that doesn't parse is never written.

**License:** MIT.

**Last activity:** The page shows 14 commits on `main` and links to an Activity tab, but it doesn't show a date for the latest commit. The repo has 0 stars and 0 forks.

**agentsync** is a Python CLI that syncs MCP server configs and rules from Claude Code to other AI coding agents. It is MIT licensed.

- **Install:** `pip install agentsync-cli`, `pipx install agentsync-cli` (the README recommends pipx for CLI tools), or `uvx agentsync-cli` to run without installing.
- **Source of truth:** There's no single canonical file. The source is your Claude Code setup: `~/.claude.json` (global MCP servers), `.mcp.json` (project MCP servers), and `CLAUDE.md` (rules).
- **Sync commands:** `agentsync sync` runs a full sync. Options include `--dry-run`, `--mcp-only`, `--rules-only`, `-t <target>`, and `--no-backup`. `agentsync validate` checks targets against the source, and `agentsync status` shows sync state and drift.
- **Supported targets:**
  - Cursor: MCP as JSON, rules as MDC.
  - Codex: MCP as TOML, rules as AGENTS.md.
  - Antigravity (Gemini): MCP as JSON, stdio servers only. There is no separate Gemini CLI adapter listed.
- **Preserving other settings:** The page doesn't state this directly. The Codex adapter uses "marker-based" writes to `config.toml`, which suggests it edits only its own section, but that's an inference.
- **Backups and dry-run:** Backups are created automatically before every write unless you pass `--no-backup`. `--dry-run` previews changes without writing.
- **Last activity:** The captured page doesn't show a last commit date. It lists 12 commits on `main`, a CHANGELOG, and one open pull request. The repo has 4 stars and 0 forks.

**Install:** Run `uv tool install git+https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare.git`, or clone the repo and run `uv tool install .` from it.

**Canonical file:** A master `mcp.json` in the `source` directory set in `~/.config/mcpshare/config.yaml`. `mcpshare pull` merges server entries from the tools listed in `init-source` into it, and `mcpshare sync` distributes it to each target.

**Commands:**
- `init` creates the config and master directory.
- `pull` collects servers into the master file without writing to targets.
- `sync` writes the master file to all configured targets, converting to each tool's format.
- `status` shows master servers, the `init-source` list, and whether each target file exists.
- `enable` and `disable` manage per-server, per-IDE disable state in `mcp.disabled.yaml`.

**Supported targets:** Claude Code, VSCode, Copilot CLI, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and OpenCode. For Claude Code, the target is `~/.claude`, and servers are written to `~/.claude.json`.

**Preserves other settings:** Yes. Only the MCP servers section is replaced. Other keys are kept, such as VSCode's `inputs`, Claude's state in `~/.claude.json`, Gemini and OpenCode settings, and non-MCP Codex TOML sections. Writes are atomic, preserve file permissions, and go through symlinks. Files with malformed JSON or TOML are skipped rather than overwritten.

**Backups and dry-run:** The page doesn't mention either option.

**License:** The page doesn't show a license.

content.content:
**sync-agents-settings** syncs MCP server configs and CLAUDE.md instructions from Claude Code to other AI coding agents.

- **Install:** As a Claude Code plugin, run `claude plugin marketplace add Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings`, then `claude plugin install sync-agents-settings`. Or run it without installing via `npx sync-agents-settings`, or install globally with `npm install -g sync-agents-settings` and use the `sync-agents` command.
- **Source of truth:** Claude Code is the origin. The tool reads `~/.claude.json` and enabled plugin `.mcp.json` files, then writes to each target's format.
- **Sync commands:** `sync-agents sync` pushes MCP configs, and `--target` limits it to specific agents. `sync-instructions` converts CLAUDE.md for other agents. `list`, `diff`, `doctor`, `validate`, and `reconcile` help you inspect and check drift.
- **Gemini and Codex:** Gemini CLI settings go to `~/.gemini/settings.json`, with HTTP URLs mapped to `httpUrl` and env var syntax converted. Codex CLI settings go to `~/.codex/config.toml` as TOML, with `${VAR:-default}` expanded. Codex defaults to global config, and `--codex-home` targets a project. Codex doesn't merge global and project configs.
- **Preserves other settings:** Existing servers are never overwritten, so re-running is safe. When a target instruction file exists, you can choose to overwrite, append, or skip.
- **Backups and dry-run:** Each sync backs up affected files to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/` unless you pass `--no-backup`. `--dry-run` previews changes without writing files.
- **License:** MIT.

content.text:
I'd go with **mcpshare**. It's the only tool I found that keeps a separate master list of your MCP servers and pushes it into Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI. Most similar tools treat Claude Code's own config as the master copy instead.

I'm assuming you're on macOS (that's what this machine reports) and that you want your global, user-level configs synced rather than per-project ones. I haven't installed or tested any of these tools; everything below comes from their READMEs. pickfit, the tool-recommendation service I checked first, had no tested tool for this job.

## Recommendation: mcpshare

**Why it fits:**
- **One list:** your servers live in a single `mcp.json` file in a folder you choose. `mcpshare sync` converts that list into each agent's format: `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code, `~/.codex/config.toml` (TOML) for Codex, and `~/.gemini/settings.json` for Gemini. It also supports VS Code, Copilot CLI, Antigravity and OpenCode.
- **Leaves your other settings alone:** it replaces only the MCP servers section of each file. Other keys and non-MCP sections of Codex's TOML file stay as they are. If a config file is broken, it skips that file instead of overwriting it.
- **Local, free, no account:** it's a Python CLI that only edits files on your machine.
- **Bonus:** you can turn a server off for one agent only (`enable` / `disable`).

**Caveats:**
- The README doesn't mention a dry-run mode or automatic backups, so make your own backup before the first sync.
- The repo page doesn't show a license, and it's a small community project.

### Install
You need `uv`. If you don't have it, run `brew install uv`.
```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare.git
```

### First run
```bash
# 0. Back up your current configs (mcpshare doesn't mention backups)
cp ~/.claude.json ~/.claude.json.bak
cp ~/.codex/config.toml ~/.codex/config.toml.bak
cp ~/.gemini/settings.json ~/.gemini/settings.json.bak

# 1. Create ~/.config/mcpshare/config.yaml and the folder for your master list
mcpshare init

# 2. Edit ~/.config/mcpshare/config.yaml: set `source` (where the master mcp.json lives),
#    `init-source` (which agents to collect servers from) and your targets
#    (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI)

# 3. Copy the servers you already have into the master mcp.json (doesn't change the agents' configs)
mcpshare pull

# 4. Check the master list and the targets
mcpshare status

# 5. Write the list to all three agents
mcpshare sync
```
After that, to add a server: put it in the master `mcp.json` and run `mcpshare sync`. To check the result, run `claude mcp list` and `codex mcp list`, and `/mcp` inside Gemini CLI.

## Alternatives
- **[mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport)** (MIT, `npm i -g mcpport`, needs Node 22+): the most careful about writing files. It previews changes unless you pass `--apply`, makes a timestamped `.bak` before each write, keeps comments in Codex's TOML, and won't rewrite a Gemini file that has comments. But it copies between agents (e.g. `mcpport sync claude codex --apply`) rather than keeping one master list. It's also brand new (0 stars). Even if you use mcpshare, it's handy for checking configs and spotting differences.
- **[sync-agents-settings](https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings)** (MIT, `npx sync-agents-settings`): treats Claude Code as the master copy and syncs to Gemini and Codex. It has `--dry-run`, automatic backups, and `diff` / `reconcile` commands. One catch: it never overwrites a server that already exists in a target, so if you change a server's settings, the change won't reach the other agents on its own.
- **[agentsync](https://github.com/spyrae/agentsync)** (MIT, `pipx install agentsync-cli`): also uses Claude Code as the master. It doesn't list a Gemini CLI adapter (only Antigravity), so it's not a good fit here.
